主要内容: Standard & Poor’s (S&P), a unit of McGraw Hill Financial Inc., has agreed to pay a $1.5 billion fine to settle legal disputes with the U.S. Justice Department, more than a dozen states, and the largest U.S. pension fund. The settlement, which does not involve an admission of wrongdoing, marks the end of a costly legal battle over the company’s ratings of subprime-mortgage bonds at the center of the 2008 financial crisis. The fine, which exceeds a year’s profit for the company, is higher than the penalties paid by major banks that created those securities. This settlement will allow S&P to move past the legal challenges and potentially close the profit gap with its main competitor, Moody’s Corp.
